title: LiDAR Utrecht, physical NFT series
location: NAR Café der Kunsten, Utrecht · Creative Coding Utrecht
excerpt: A series of light sculptures that translate raw LiDAR point clouds of Utrecht landmarks into laser-cut, backlit wood.
description:
> On the interface between the physical world and cyberspace, I make art that brings the two universes together. The LiDAR series interprets raw aerial LiDAR data of Utrecht into physical objects: point clouds of the city's landmarks engraved by laser into wood and lit from within by LED, framed in aluminium.
Each piece is 300×300mm and captures a single Utrecht location from a chosen perspective in 3D space. Up close the buildings dissolve into thousands of luminous points, and every wall becomes light. The first five works in the series are Tivoli Vredenburg (5.1), the Stadskantoor (5.2), the Neude library (5.3), the windmill on the Adelaarstraat (5.4), and the Nijverheid / Havenloods (5.6).
Presented as “physical NFTs”, each sculpture is paired with a digital token that registers it, exploring the boundary between digital and physical art, and the shifting role of accessibility and ownership in a digitalising world.
The series was first shown in Math Expressionism, an exhibition of work by the international community of creative coders, held at NAR Café der Kunsten in Utrecht. Alongside the work the programme ran workshops and discussions on NFTs, where makers shared their experience of communities like Hic et Nunc and Artblocks, and the controversies around them.
credits: Physical NFT series. Laser-cut wood, engraved LiDAR point cloud, LED light, aluminium frame, 300×300mm. Point clouds derived from aerial LiDAR data of Utrecht. Shown in Math Expressionism, presented by Creative Coding Utrecht at NAR Café der Kunsten, Utrecht, made possible with the support of the Creative Industries Fund NL, Gemeente Utrecht and TheElephantNL. Also shown at Aquí y Ahora, Arthouse Pani, Tequisquiapan, curated by Santiago Pani.
